kiidp-kampala-roads-compensation.confidence_note: The figures of 494 compensated and 239 unpaid still rest entirely on the Independent Evaluation Group's review of a completion report the Bank has not disclosed. Round 41 searched the two outside routes that exist for this project and neither reaches it. ULII's search index, which also carries Ugandan legislation, gazettes and parliamentary Hansard, returns nothing at all for "Kampala Institutional and Infrastructure Development" or "KIIDP" (0 documents each), and its nine documents on "Lubigi" are a murder trial, a gazette boundary description, three Hansard sittings of 2024 and 2025, an environmental injunction and one compensation case: Swacoff Inter-Trade (U) Ltd v Kampala Capital City Authority, in which the court records that in HCCS 714 of 2016 Vivo Energy sued the Authority for UGX 2.26 billion over land acquired for Lubigi drainage works. bukoba-airport-resettlement-arrears.confidence_note: Two records outside the lender now carry this card's harm. Tanzania's Controller and Auditor General, in the annual audit of development projects for the year ended 30 June 2017 (AGR/DP/2016/2017) — the project's own closing year — reports that people affected by three projects had not been paid compensation totalling TZS 11,870,767,751, and its schedule 1(i) lists the Transport Sector Support Project, which the same report identifies as World Bank funded, at TZS 36,826,419 unpaid. That is the card's harm, unpaid compensation under this project at its close, on the state auditor's record rather than the Bank's. The audit does not break the figure down by site, so attributing it to Bukoba is an inference from the completion report's own account that no resettlement was required on the roads or at Tabora and Kigoma and that Zanzibar was complete, which leaves Bukoba as the only site with cases pending. Second, the High Court of Tanzania at Bukoba decided Land Case No. 6B of 2010, Regina Peter Kamugisha vs Airport Manager Bukoba Airport & others, on 10 May 2018, eleven months after the credits closed. Everything known about that judgment comes from TanzLII's search index and its highlighted page snippets: the judgment itself cannot be opened, because TanzLII's document pages answer HTTP 403 behind Cloudflare, so nothing here may be treated as read from the judgment. What the index carries: the suit was instituted on 11/10/2010 and the court sat on 9 and 10 May 2018; a snippet describes the plaintiff as "a widow and reside of Kashai, Municipality of Bukoba", aged 59, suing as administratrix of the estate of Peter Kamugisha; the defendants named on page 1 are the Airport Manager, Bukoba Airport, the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Infrastructure & Development and the Attorney General, with Kagera Co-operative Union (1990) Ltd as third party; the dispute follows government acquisition of plot No. 142 Block "Z" Bukoba Municipality, where the snippet says the first defendant paid someone else; a snippet records the third party being paid a grand total of TZS 132,330,000 in compensation for 4,768 square metres, and the whole compensation schedule, covering plot numbers 109 to 145 in the Kashai area of Bukoba Municipality, going in as exhibit D2; she claimed TZS 10,000,000 more for disturbance; and TanzLII's own case note says a registered owner is entitled to compensation where the state paid a third party without proper title, with the building and general damages awarded. No document found says this is one of the five cases the completion report counted, and the Bank's documents give no case numbers. The completion report's other claims — that the school move was largely successful, that the quarry families asked to move and were satisfied, that Zanzibar was complete — are still only the lender's.

kenya-1991-university-fees-esac.confidence_note: This is a 1991 structural-adjustment case and the judgment indexes cannot hold it; recording their silence would be recording nothing. Kenya Law's earliest 1991 material is legal-notice metadata (for example Income Tax Act exemption notices published in Kenya Gazette Vol. XCIII), with no gazette text and no judgments of the period, and the National Assembly's online Hansard is the current session only, so neither Hansard nor the national archives, whose site did not serve, could be searched for the 1991 fee debate. Outside the lender, one contemporaneous official record was found and it corrects the card. The United States Department of State's Country Report on Human Rights Practices for 1991, published in February 1992, records that on 30 June, during a riot over student allowances, "one Moi University student, Shadrack Opiyo, was shot dead by the police". It adds that no investigation followed. That is the same date and the same single death as the event the Social Conflict Analysis Database codes, which the card describes as a nationwide protest against the raising of university fees; the identification is inferred from date and death count, not stated by either source. The grievance, on the outside record, is student allowances rather than fees, and the place is Moi University rather than nationwide or Nairobi; the card's point sits at Nairobi. The fee itself is corroborated outside the lender by a Kenyan academic record: Okuro, "Financing Higher Education in Kenya, 1960-2012", East African Journal of Education Studies 7(4), 2024, which dates a radical policy shift to 1991, attributes it partly to continued World Bank and IMF pressure to cut state funding of higher education, and says that in the 1991-92 academic year "the government for the first time introduced the cost-sharing or user charges scheme" requiring public university students to pay fees. That is a journal article, not a judgment, audit or newspaper, so it strengthens the card without moving it. The KSh 6,000 figure, the Board-presentation condition and the 1995 tranche terms remain the lender's own.

The two records share a date and a single death, so they are probably the same event, but neither says so, and the State Department gives the grievance as student allowances and the place as Moi University, not fees and not Nairobi.
field_changes.killed_note: Not counted. The Social Conflict Analysis Database codes one death in the protest of 30 June-1 July 1991. The United States Department of State's Country Report on Human Rights Practices for 1991 names that death: Shadrack Opiyo, a Moi University student, shot dead by the police on 30 June 1991 during a riot over student allowances, with no investigation following. The death is therefore no longer unconfirmed, and it was caused by the police. It is still not counted here because the outside record gives the grievance as student allowances rather than the fee the credit required, and no document ties the shooting to the credit's conditions.

corrections: The card's suppression field says "No news report of this protest was found to confirm it." A contemporaneous official record does confirm a death on that date and names the person: the US State Department's human rights report for 1991 gives Shadrack Opiyo, a Moi University student, shot dead by police on 30 June 1991, with no investigation following.

The card describes the event as a protest against the raising of university fees. The outside record gives the grievance as student allowances, and the place as Moi University in Eldoret rather than the nationwide protest the dataset codes or the Nairobi point the card uses. The Bank's own credit touched both, since it introduced the KSh 6,000 charge and capped student loans at KSh 21,500, but the two sources do not describe the same grievance and the card should not present the death as a death over fees.
kenya-1991-university-fees-esac.what_the_outside_source_settles: That a student was shot dead by Kenyan police on 30 June 1991 in a university riot, who he was, where he studied, and that no investigation followed; and, from a Kenyan academic source, that direct fees at public universities began in the 1991-92 academic year under World Bank and IMF pressure to cut state funding of higher education.
kenya-1991-university-fees-esac.what_it_does_not_settle: Whether the dataset's event and the State Department's shooting are the same event, which rests on the shared date and the single death. Whether the riot was over the new fee, the capped loan, the cut allowance or all three. Everything specific to the credit: the KSh 6,000 charge as a condition of Board presentation, the third-tranche terms of up to KSh 50,000 and a minimum KSh 8,000, the arrears from 1992/93 and the "negligible" rating on loan reform are all from the Bank's own implementation completion report, which no outside document checks.
